description: The plot titled “Massive Activation of baseline” illustrates how the maximum activation value varies across model layers for four signals (attn_output, attn_residual, ffn_output, ffn_residual). The x-axis is labeled “Layer,” uses a linear scale, and spans approximately layers 0 to 23 with major ticks shown at 0, 5, 10, 15, and 20. The y-axis is labeled “Max Activation Value,” uses a linear scale, and ranges from 0 to 1600 with regularly spaced tick marks every 200 units. The blue dashed line (attn_output) stays near 0 for most layers and then rises late, reaching roughly ~250 by the final layer. The orange dotted line (attn_residual) is near 0 through about layer 4, jumps sharply to around ~1400 at about layer 5, remains high around ~1450–1600 through roughly layers 6–21, then drops steeply near layer 22 to around ~600 and ends near ~1500 at the last layer. The green dash-dot line (ffn_output) is near 0 early, shows a sharp spike around layer 5 up to roughly ~1300, returns close to 0 by around layers 7–11, spikes again around layer 13 to roughly ~700, declines back toward near-0 by around layers 15–20, then spikes again near layer 22 to roughly ~1200 before dropping back down by the final layer. The red solid line (ffn_residual) is near 0 through about layer 4, jumps to about ~1400 at around layer 5, stays elevated around ~1500–1600 through roughly layers 6–21, then drops sharply near layer 22 to around ~400 and rises to about ~600 by the final layer.
